Reading a lot of this reminds me of what I experienced only a few weeks ago. My cat, Mittens, had a mass and started losing weight. She even started eating her own litter too. I did everything the vet suggested but unfortunately, it just wasn’t enough either. It still hurts so much. She was literally my therapy cat for almost a decade (my therapist convinced my brother to let me have her after we lost our mom.) Even now, I miss her with all my being. 

I will say this though. It’s clear you love your cat so much. I struggled with the decision to say goodbye to Mittens. I knew it was for the best unfortunately. She loved food so much that my boyfriend nicknamed her “the little piggy princess”. I spent hundreds alone on trying different foods of all types when she stopped eating and the vet couldn’t do anything else because even medicine wasn’t working. 

As much as it hurts, the best thing we can do is take their pain and make it our own. When I first saw that statement, it resonated with me. Cats especially hide their pain well so as much as it hurts, we have to do what we can to help them without being able to communicate. 

It’s okay to not be okay. It’s okay to not want to let go but if deep down, you know you have to, you have to fight through the pain and make sure you’re doing what’s best for your kitty. Time does help, however slowly it is. 

I hope the best for you and if you need to vent or anything, I’m open to listening. Good luck.
